2751.def:
// Article-specific bespoke detection — VEIL#DROP Malware Chain Uses Blogger Platform to Deliver PureLogs Stealer
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named
// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("transcript.pdf.js", "regsvcs.exe", "installutil.exe", "msbuild.exe", "aspnet_compiler.exe"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

// File-creation events for the named binaries / paths
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (FileName in~ ("transcript.pdf.js", "regsvcs.exe", "installutil.exe", "msbuild.exe", "aspnet_compiler.exe"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
2751.spl:
``` Article-specific bespoke detection — VEIL#DROP Malware Chain Uses Blogger Platform to Deliver PureLogs Stealer ```
| tstats `summariesonly` count earliest(_time) AS firstTime latest(_time) AS lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process_name IN ("transcript.pdf.js","regsvcs.exe","installutil.exe","msbuild.exe","aspnet_compiler.exe"))
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name,
       Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_path
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| append [
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("created","modified")
      AND (Filesystem.file_name IN ("transcript.pdf.js","regsvcs.exe","installutil.exe","msbuild.exe","aspnet_compiler.exe"))

2801.def:
// Article-specific bespoke detection — Securing AI agents: When AI tools move from reading to acting
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named
// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("node.js"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

// File-creation events for the named binaries / paths
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (FileName in~ ("node.js"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
2801.spl:
``` Article-specific bespoke detection — Securing AI agents: When AI tools move from reading to acting ```
| tstats `summariesonly` count earliest(_time) AS firstTime latest(_time) AS lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process_name IN ("node.js"))
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name,
       Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_path
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| append [
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("created","modified")
      AND (Filesystem.file_name IN ("node.js"))
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, Filesystem.process_name,
       Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.file_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
]

  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/guardfall-exposes-open-source-ai-coding.html
  - https://adversa.ai/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/30
tags:
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1059
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_agent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/aider'
      - '/goose'
      - '/cline'
      - '/plandex'
      - '/opencode'
      - '/open-interpreter'
      - '/openhands'
      - '/swe-agent'
      - '/interpreter'
    ParentCommandLine|contains:
      - '--auto-exec'
      - '--auto-run'
      - '--auto-test'
      - '--yes-always'
      - '--no-confirm'
      - 'dangerously-skip-permissions'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/dash'
      - '/zsh'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
  condition: selection_agent and selection_child
level: medium

2833.sent:
let lookback = 7d;
let window = 1h;
let Failed = CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where DeviceVendor =~ "Fortinet"
| where Activity has "login" and (EventOutcome in~ ("failure","failed") or Message has_any ("login failed","Login failed","authentication failed","ssl-login-fail"))
| summarize Failures = count(), TargetUsers = dcount(DestinationHostName) by SourceIP, bin(TimeGenerated, window);
let Success = CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where DeviceVendor =~ "Fortinet"
| where Activity has "login" and (EventOutcome in~ ("success","succeeded") or Message has_any ("login successful","SSL tunnel established"))
| summarize Successes = count(), CompromisedUser = make_set(DestinationHostName, 20) by SourceIP, bin(TimeGenerated, window);
Failed
| where Failures >= 30   // 30 = empirical spray burst floor per source per hour
| join kind=inner Success on SourceIP, TimeGenerated
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, Failures, TargetUsers, Successes, CompromisedUser
| order by Failures desc
2833.spl:
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.app IN ("fortios","fortigate","fortiproxy","ftnt-fortigate","sslvpn-plain","forticlient_ems") by Authentication.src, Authentication.dest, Authentication.user, Authentication.action, _time span=1h
| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
| stats sum(eval(if(action="failure",count,0))) as failures, sum(eval(if(action="success",count,0))) as successes, dc(user) as targeted_users, values(eval(if(action="success",user,null()))) as compromised_user, values(dest) as dest by src, _time
| where failures >= 30 and successes >= 1
| sort - failures

  - https://blog.talosintelligence.com/hypotheses-telemetry-and-human-judgment-inside-cisco-talos-threat-hunting/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/04
tags:
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.execution
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
  selection_fetch:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'Invoke-WebRequest'
      - 'iwr '
      - 'Net.WebClient'
      - 'DownloadFile'
      - 'DownloadString'
  selection_file:
    CommandLine|contains: 'script.ps1'
  selection_path:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'AppData'
      - 'ApplicationData'
      - '\Roaming\'
      - '\Local\'
  condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate internal scripts that happen to fetch a file named script.ps1 into AppData (rare; review user context)
level: high
2990.spl:
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdlines values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parents from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") (Processes.process="*Invoke-WebRequest*" OR Processes.process="*iwr *" OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*") Processes.process="*script.ps1*" (Processes.process="*AppData*" OR Processes.process="*ApplicationData*" OR Processes.process="*\\Roaming\\*" OR Processes.process="*\\Local\\*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
2990.datadog: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\pwsh.exe)) AND (@CommandLine:(*Invoke-WebRequest* OR *iwr\ * OR *Net.WebClient* OR *DownloadFile* OR *DownloadString*)) AND @CommandLine:*script.ps1* AND (@CommandLine:(*AppData* OR *ApplicationData* OR *\\Roaming\\* OR *\\Local\\*))
2990.falcon:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i
| regex("(Invoke-WebRequest|iwr |Net\.WebClient|DownloadFile|DownloadString)", field=CommandLine)
| regex("script\.ps1", field=CommandLine)
| regex("(AppData|ApplicationData|\\\\Roaming\\\\|\\\\Local\\\\)", field=CommandLine)

| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

2991.def:

| where RemoteIP == "144.31.221.82" or (RemotePort == 6060 and RemoteUrl has "/capcha")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "curl.exe")
| summarize ProcessSet = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName),
            FirstConnection = min(Timestamp),
            LastConnection = max(Timestamp),
            ConnectionCount = count(),
            CmdLines = make_set(InitiatingProcessCommandLine, 8)
          by DeviceId, DeviceName, RemoteIP, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName

2991.sent:
let WindowHours = 1h;
let FirewallHits = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where DestinationIP == "144.31.221.82" or (DestinationPort == 6060 and RequestURL has "/capcha")
    | project FirewallTime=TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, RequestURL;
let ProcessHits = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName endswith "\\powershell.exe"
         or NewProcessName endswith "\\pwsh.exe"
         or NewProcessName endswith "\\curl.exe"
    | where CommandLine has_any ("144.31.221.82", "capcha", "script.ps1")
         or NewProcessName endswith "\\curl.exe"
    | project ProcessTime=TimeGenerated, Computer, NewProcessName, CommandLine, SubjectUserName;
FirewallHits
| join kind=inner (
    ProcessHits
    | summarize Procs=make_set(NewProcessName), AnyCmd=make_set(CommandLine, 8) by Computer
    | where array_length(Procs) >= 2
) on $left.SourceIP == $right.Computer
| order by FirewallTime desc

// Article-specific bespoke detection — Node-gyp Supply Chain Compromise: A Self-Propagating npm Worm That Hides in bind

| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","node.exe","python","python3","node")
| where FileName in~ ("aws.exe","aws","kubectl.exe","kubectl")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("ssm send-command","ssm start-session","kubectl exec","exec -it","exec --stdin")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

2999.sigma:
title: AWS SSM SendCommand or kubectl exec spawned by Python/Node runtime
id: 7c1d4b29-a6e8-4f93-bb12-2e8f5a90d147
status: experimental
description: Catches the durabletask post-compromise tradecraft where a backdoored Python (or node) interpreter shells out to aws/kubectl to move laterally via SSM SendCommand/StartSession or kubectl exec using the victim's own cloud credentials.
references:
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/edr-proxy-wont-protect-supply-chain-malware
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/03
tags:
  - attack.t1021.007
  - attack.t1609
  - attack.lateral_movement
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
      - '/node'
      - '\python.exe'
      - '\python3.exe'
      - '\node.exe'
  child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/aws'
      - '/kubectl'
      - '\aws.exe'
      - '\kubectl.exe'
  cmdline:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'ssm send-command'
      - 'ssm start-session'
      - 'kubectl exec'
      - 'exec -it'
  condition: parent and child and cmdline
level: high
2999.spl: | tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("python.exe","python3.exe","node.exe","python","python3","node") AND Processes.process_name IN ("aws.exe","aws","kubectl.exe","kubectl") AND (Processes.process="*ssm send-command*" OR Processes.process="*ssm start-session*" OR Processes.process="*kubectl exec*" OR Processes.process="*exec -it*" OR Processes.process="*exec --stdin*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
2999.datadog: source:cloudtrail @eventSource:ssm.amazonaws.com @evt.name:(SendCommand OR StartSession) @evt.outcome:success (@userAgent:*python* OR @userAgent:*Boto3* OR @userAgent:*aws-sdk-nodejs* OR @userAgent:*node-fetch*)
2999.falcon:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/(python3?|node)(\.exe)?$/i ImageFileName=/(aws|kubectl)(\.exe)?$/i
| regex("ssm send-command|ssm start-session|kubectl exec|exec -it", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
2999.cloudwatch:
# log group: /aws/cloudtrail
fields @timestamp, eventName, eventSource, userIdentity.type, userIdentity.arn, userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.userName, sourceIPAddress, userAgent, requestParameters.documentName, requestParameters.target
| filter eventSource = "ssm.amazonaws.com"
      and eventName in ["SendCommand", "StartSession"]
      and not isPresent(errorCode)
      and (userAgent like /python/i or userAgent like /Boto3/i or userAgent like /aws-sdk-nodejs/i)
| sort @timestamp desc
